about: Where the two answers in tour/data/relocation-R009-sealed.jsonl come from. Stop 9 prints this record at the top of its output and checks the two rows against it; tests/test_tour.py checks the commits named here.

set.kept: read-only in the project's private working records, never committed to a repository

written.how: wrote the cases, the questions and these answers itself, from the policy's text and its written instructions only; it never saw the translation

translation_frozen.before: any question or answer of the set existed

after_the_seal: The tour runs a later commit (tour/AFTER_RELEASE_COMMIT): the frozen translation plus one fix made after grading, for another case's question (a missing written pre-approval it had ignored). At the frozen commit, case R009's two answers were the same (no, no).
who_could_read: Rules, not locks: the set sits read-only on the project's machine, where any of the project's AI sessions could have opened it. By the run's written rules, the session that translated the policy never read it. The session that turned the questions into facts read only the questions until that work was committed (25 Nov 2026, 19:53 UTC); it then ran the grading program and saw the grades. Two fresh AI sessions that built nothing judged 24 of the answers, a later check of the grading read the set, and the two rows here were copied from it. The grades, which quote the sealed answers, were open to the sessions that fixed the translation after grading.

first_commit_here.subject: tour: ten stop scripts, install script, club text

commit_ids: the project's own repository; a published copy of its history has other IDs
